prompts.title: What are you working on right now?
prompts.hint: A-IEP, the evaluation work, the portfolio, whatever is actually on your mind.

prompts.title: Explain A-IEP to a friend who has never heard of it.
prompts.hint: Parents get a fifty-page plan; it turns it into plain language, in their own language; names get stripped out first.

prompts.title: What happened with the Acharya app?
prompts.hint: You took it over at a 1.2 rating, users kept growing, what broke, what you fixed.

prompts.title: Tell me about your setup, or the last thing you played.
prompts.hint: PC builds, keyboards, Valorant, CS2. Whatever you would ramble about.

prompts.title: A founder just joined the call. What do you tell them in the first thirty seconds?
prompts.hint: Say it the way you actually would.

prompts.title: Read this casually. Change any word you would not say.
prompts.text: So, quick numbers. A-IEP has read three hundred seventy-five plans so far, and it runs in four languages. On the Acharya app, monthly users went from two thousand nine hundred seventy-two to sixteen thousand one hundred forty-eight while I owned it, and the rating went from one point two to four point five. GENIE gave forty-four thousand state employees access to AI, and the router I wrote picks between seventeen models. At the AWS and Riot Games hackathon, we came second out of more than three thousand two hundred people.

prompts.title: Read this like you mean it.
prompts.text: Wait, is that right? Yeah, second. Honestly, still a little annoyed about that. Anyway. Want to see something I built? Ask me anything, I'll show you.
